options: A sail drive through the hull
A water jet pump in the hull
An engine and propeller unit hung on the transom
An engine fixed inside the hull driving a propeller shaft
questions.explanation: It steers by turning the whole unit.

options: Steering that works best when stopped
A very long shaft and a large, slow-turning propeller
No propeller; steering needs water flowing out
Two rudders behind the jet nozzle
questions.explanation: Without thrust there is no steering.

questions.stem: Before starting an inboard gasoline engine you should:
options: Switch off the battery switch
Pump the bilge dry with the engine
Open the fuel valve fully and prime
Run the bilge blower and check for fuel vapour
questions.explanation: Vapour in the bilge can explode.

questions.stem: The kill-switch lanyard is attached to:
options: The dock
The operator
The anchor
The fuel tank
questions.explanation: If the operator falls away, the engine stops.

questions.stem: Low oil pressure on a running engine means you should:
options: Reduce power and stop the engine promptly
Keep going and check it at the dock
Add coolant to the expansion tank
Increase speed to raise the oil pressure again
questions.explanation: An engine can be ruined in seconds without oil.

questions.stem: After starting an outboard you should check that:
options: The fuel gauge reads full
The radio and lights are on
Cooling water is coming out
The anchor is stowed
questions.explanation: No cooling water quickly overheats the engine.

questions.stem: Before applying the gear lever at start-up you should make sure it is in:
options: Full ahead
Any position
Neutral
Full astern
questions.explanation: The engine should start in neutral.

options: An inboard engine driving a leg outside the transom
A sail rig with an auxiliary motor
A water jet pump inside the hull
An outboard with a long shaft
questions.explanation: It combines an inboard engine with an outdrive.

questions.stem: If the engine temperature alarm sounds you should first:
options: Open the radiator cap on the hot engine
Switch off the bilge pump
Reduce power and check the cooling water flow
Increase speed to push more cooling water through
questions.explanation: Overheating can be caused by blocked intakes or low coolant.
